$comment: INTERIM nav/search data for the port-docs lane. Extracted verbatim from the Next site's data/elements.json + reference-glossary.ts + reference-buckets.ts (landing-preview worktree) by lane port-docs on 2026-10-14. Long-term source: port-reference's compile-time modules generated from the npl-enhanced-content subtree (Semtext.Reference.*) — converge on those and retire this file once they land (see the port-docs lane report, cross-lane requests).

tags.name: agent
tags.summary: Document-level metadata aimed at a model: name, bio, instructions.
tags.description: The tag form is bare <agent> (Appendix A maps it to div.sem-agent); extraction names the record type sem-agent. Inert to the browser, a record to the extractor.

tags.name: conclusion
tags.summary: Fact part — the citable takeaway extraction returns.
tags.description: Bare semantic child of sem-fact; any inline content. Conclusions are verbatim-citable assertions; distractors never are.

tags.name: highlight
tags.summary: Prose with occludable content.
tags.description: Prose with occludable content. Recall-oriented prose, distinct from `sem-reveal` (block disclosure) and `sem-views` (perspective switching): same prose, a different interaction model per view. Each `sem-detail` is one prose passage; a `<highlight>` child marks a recall target (`[[cloze]]` sugar maps to `<highlight>`) — `<em>` in plain view, occluded and revealed per item in the `quiz` view (self-check model). `view-as` is display-only sugar (`plain` default, `quiz`): the prose is identical under both.

tags.name: incorrect-statement
tags.summary: Explicit wrong candidate for quiz view; never extracted as a claim.
tags.description: Child of sem-fact; quiz view only. Up to 3 distractors win over sibling conclusions when the quiz builds its options; with scripts off they render labelled, hidden by nothing.

tags.name: npl-agent
tags.summary: Agent definition card: the element form of the NPL agent convention's `⌜name|type|NPL@version⌝ … ⌞name⌟` header.
tags.description: Agent definition card: the element form of the NPL agent convention's `⌜name|type|NPL@version⌝ … ⌞name⌟` header. The three header fields become attributes; the authored prose (the description and behavioural spec) stays the body and is never rewritten. Display-only (Lit `NplAgent`, `src/lit/npl/npl-agent.ts`).

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required. The agent's identifier, the `⌜<agent-name>` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-name` after upgrade (the resolved value — an authored `data-name` is never overwritten).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: required. The agent's archetype (e.g. `scout`, `coder`). Mirrored to `data-type` after upgrade (the resolved value).

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: required. The NPL contract version, the `NPL@{version}` field of the source form. Mirrored to `data-version` after upgrade (the resolved value).

attributes.name: extends
attributes.description: optional. The parent agent this definition extends; the header omits it when not authored. Mirrored to `data-extends` after upgrade (the resolved value).

tags.name: npl-artifact
tags.summary: A structured output block with metadata — the display of an artifact an NPL agent emits (generated code, a report, a figure).
tags.description: A structured output block with metadata — the display of an artifact an NPL agent emits (generated code, a report, a figure). Display-only: no events, no state; the authored children carry the data and the upgrade turns them into display chrome in place (`title` becomes the heading, `content` becomes preformatted text, or a sandboxed iframe when `type="svg"`) — Lit `NplArtifact`, `src/lit/npl/npl-artifact.ts`.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: (unset). A content type such as `text`, `code`, `svg`, `markdown`. `svg` routes the content through a sandboxed iframe; every other value (including unset) renders the content preformatted. Mirrored to `data-type` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse).

tags.name: npl-cot
tags.summary: Chain-of-thought block: the steps of an NPL `cot` block's `thought_process` plus its outcome, folded in a native `<details>`.
tags.description: Chain-of-thought block: the steps of an NPL `cot` block's `thought_process` plus its outcome, folded in a native `<details>`. Lit component: `src/lit/npl/npl-cot.ts`; toggle is native, so it works without JavaScript.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: Absent ⇒ the block starts expanded; present ⇒ it starts collapsed. Sets the **initial** open state of the native details; the user's own toggling is never re-forced. The runtime mirrors the boolean to `data-collapsed` (`"true"`/`"false"`) in `updated()` via afterParse — a write for CSS/extraction parity, never an input (the component reads the bare attribute only, like the sem tier's `collapsed`); the mirror is deferred past parse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes.

tags.name: npl-critique
tags.summary: Structured critique of one subject from one perspective, with strengths, weaknesses, and a verdict.
tags.description: Structured critique of one subject from one perspective, with strengths, weaknesses, and a verdict. Source: NPL critique blocks. Display-only — the component structures authored children; it hides nothing, fires nothing, and owns no state (Lit `NplCritique`, `src/lit/npl/npl-critique.ts`).

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: per the global attribute catalog — optional, the native HTML `id`; the only attribute parameter. No component-specific parameters exist; all content rides the five authored children.

tags.name: npl-declaration
tags.summary: Display-only banner for an NPL declaration block: the version/extension header of a rules document (`src/lit/npl/npl-declaration.ts`).
tags.description: Display-only banner for an NPL declaration block: the version/extension header of a rules document (`src/lit/npl/npl-declaration.ts`). The source forms are the NPL fences `⌜NPL@<version>⌝ … ⌞NPL@⌟` (definition) and `⌜extend:NPL@<version>⌝ … ⌞NPL@⌟` (extension); the component renders the banner text the source spells, with the rules content as authored children.

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: required; a missing version warns and the banner still renders, with the bare mark (`⌜NPL@⌝`). Rendered in the banner mark (`⌜NPL@<version>⌝`) and mirrored to `data-version` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: one of `definition` | `extension`. Selects the banner mark (`⌜NPL@…⌝` vs `⌜extend:NPL@…⌝`) and mirrors the resolved kind to `data-type`. Any other value falls back to `definition`.

attributes.name: extend-target
attributes.description: optional; the vocabulary an extension extends, authored on `type="extension"` declarations. Rendered by `.npl-declaration-target` beside the mark whenever authored and mirrored to `data-extend-target` (absent when unauthored).

tags.name: npl-directive
tags.summary: Inline directive chip: the element form of an NPL inline directive `⟪glyph: instruction | elaboration⟫` or prefix chip `emoji➤ instruction`.
tags.description: Inline directive chip: the element form of an NPL inline directive `⟪glyph: instruction | elaboration⟫` or prefix chip `emoji➤ instruction`. Display-only (Lit `NplDirective`, `src/lit/npl/npl-directive.ts`).

attributes.name: glyph
attributes.description: required; the emoji or symbol leading the chip. Rendered by `.npl-directive-glyph` (dropped, gracefully, when absent) and mirrored to `data-glyph` when non-empty.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: one of `directive` | `prefix`. A `prefix` chip renders the `➤` arrow between glyph and instruction, the prefix form's source grammar. Mirrored to `data-kind` (resolved value).

attributes.name: qualifier
attributes.description: optional; a trailing label beside the instruction, rendered by `.npl-directive-qualifier` and mirrored to `data-qualifier` when non-empty.

tags.name: npl-example
tags.summary: Placeholder component proving the `npl-*` pattern end to end (`src/lit/npl/npl-example.ts`).
tags.description: Placeholder component proving the `npl-*` pattern end to end (`src/lit/npl/npl-example.ts`). Delete this file together with the component once real components exist; keep the recipe it demonstrates (`src/lit/npl/index.ts` header, `spec/schema/npl/TEMPLATE.md`).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Displayed by `.npl-example-label` and mirrored to `data-label` (dual-form contract: `data-label` wins when both spellings are present, so the mirror writes the resolved value and never clobbers an authored `data-label`; deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: npl-flag
tags.summary: One runtime flag row: a `name`/`value` pair rendered as one labelled row the reader can click to apply.
tags.description: One runtime flag row: a `name`/`value` pair rendered as one labelled row the reader can click to apply. Authored inside the `npl-flags` container; usable standalone. Values render verbatim; when the name implies a numeric range the value is checked against it, and an out-of-range or non-numeric value is not an error — the flag renders with the `npl-flag-invalid` warning class on its value span. Clicking the flag toggles `data-applied` on it and dispatches `npl-flags-change` to the host app.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required, no default. Flag identifier; its wording implies the numeric range checked on `value` (below).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: no default. Rendered verbatim; validated only when the name implies a numeric range (case-insensitive substring of the name): `freq` checks [0.0, 1.0] (frequency flags), `factor` checks [-10, 10] (hormone factors), `threshold` must be numeric and unbounded. Any other name (pump switches, meta, …) is free-form — never validated. An out-of-range or non-numeric value is NOT an error: the flag renders with the `npl-flag-invalid` warning class on its value span.

tags.name: npl-flags
tags.summary: Container for `npl-flag` children (`npl-flag.md`) plus optional note text.
tags.description: Container for `npl-flag` children (`npl-flag.md`) plus optional note text. Mirrors the sem-* prose contracts in `spec/schema/*.md`: prose is normative — changes here precede spec changes precede code, and this file is the BDD source of truth for `test/unit/npl-flags.test.ts`.

attributes.name: preset
attributes.description: optional, no default (omit it entirely for no badge). One of `minimal`, `full`, `production`, `creative`, `tireless` (the NPL flag source spells these `preset:<name>`; the attribute accepts the bare word or the prefixed spelling, normalized for display). An unknown preset is NOT an error: it warns through the author-facing channel and renders with the invalid-preset warning class (see Rendered form).

tags.name: npl-hormones
tags.summary: Source block: the NPL synthetic-hormones pump (NoizuPromptLingo `conventions/pumps.yaml`, `synthetic-hormones`).
tags.description: Source block: the NPL synthetic-hormones pump (NoizuPromptLingo `conventions/pumps.yaml`, `synthetic-hormones`). Seven biochemical-analog hormones — Momentum MTM, Tension TNS, Curiosity CRS, Confidence CNF, Affinity AFN, Fatigue FTG, Restlessness RST — drawn as bars with delta arrows and threshold alerts. Display-only: no events, no network, no timers.

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: `panel` renders one row per `h` plus the `state` and `triggered` lines; `bars` renders only the rows (the compact form); `alert` renders only the `alert` elements. Any other value falls back to `panel`.

attributes.name: state
attributes.description: child element — compound state description, rendered in the `panel` variant as the state line.

attributes.name: triggered
attributes.description: child element — threshold behaviors activated, or `none`. A row is highlighted (`data-fired`) when this block names the hormone: by symbol (word match, so `RST` does not hit "first"), by name, or by its `trigger` text; `none` highlights nothing.

attributes.name: alert
attributes.description: child elements — `hormone`, `value`, `threshold`, `behavior` attributes, body text as content. Rendered only by the `alert` variant.

tags.name: npl-intent
tags.summary: Display-only render of an NPL intent block: goal, scope, outcomes and an assumptions grid.
tags.description: Display-only render of an NPL intent block: goal, scope, outcomes and an assumptions grid. Lit `NplIntent` (`src/lit/npl/npl-intent.ts`); this file is the normative source of the BDD spec `test/unit/npl-intent.test.ts`.

tags.name: npl-mindread
tags.summary: Theory-of-mind reading of the other party — the display upgrade of the NPL `<npl-mindread>` block (NoizuPromptLingo `npl/npl-full.md` §3.6 Social Cognition).
tags.description: Theory-of-mind reading of the other party — the display upgrade of the NPL `<npl-mindread>` block (NoizuPromptLingo `npl/npl-full.md` §3.6 Social Cognition). Source block: ```html <npl-mindread> <subject>{who — user, collaborator, agent name}</subject> <signals> <signal type="tone|pattern|omission|context|contradiction|expertise">{observed evidence}</signal> </signals> <inferred> <motive>{goal behind the stated request}</motive> <mood>{emotional state}</mood> <cognitive>{how they're thinking}</cognitive> <unspoken>{what they need but haven't articulated}</unspoken> </inferred> <adaptation>{concrete behavioral change}</adaptation> </npl-mindread> ``` Contract per conventions.md v0.6 and the namespace recipe in `src/lit/npl/index.ts`. Display-only: no events, no interactivity.

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.description: optional, a theory-of-mind reading is a guess until corrected; authored `0..1`. Out-of-range values are **clamped** into `[0,1]` (a non-numeric authoring clamps to `0`), and the host is **marked**: `data-confidence` carries the clamped value, `data-confidence-out-of-range` the verbatim authored value, and the meter gains a `npl-mindread-confidence-out` note.

tags.name: npl-mode
tags.summary: Cognitive lens declaration (display-only): the authored `mode` children enumerate the cognitive lenses of an NPL agent; the component renders one chip per lens, marked when the declaration is primary.
tags.description: Cognitive lens declaration (display-only): the authored `mode` children enumerate the cognitive lenses of an NPL agent; the component renders one chip per lens, marked when the declaration is primary.

attributes.name: primary
attributes.description: Resolved in either authoring spelling (`data-primary` wins, conventions §2). Declares this the primary lens; marks the rendered chips (`npl-mode-chip-primary`) and mirrors to `data-primary` after parse — an authored `data-primary` is never clobbered by the default.

tags.name: npl-mood
tags.summary: Affective-state chip (display-only).
tags.description: Affective-state chip (display-only). Source: NPL mood blocks — the block's emoji and optional qualifier ride the `mood` attribute; its tone, context and approach annotations ride optional children.

attributes.name: mood
attributes.description: required. One emoji followed by an optional qualifier string, whitespace-separated (`"🙂 wistful"`); a lone emoji is valid. Displayed by `.npl-mood-chip` and mirrored to `data-mood` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: npl-poa
tags.summary: The NPL plan-of-action block: a decision tree with weighted reasoning.
tags.description: The NPL plan-of-action block: a decision tree with weighted reasoning. Source is the NPL `poa` block — a ```mermaid fence for the decision tree, a `<reasoning>` element with the weighted paths, and a `<selected>` element naming the chosen option. Display-only: the component never loads mermaid or any runtime library, so the tree degrades to its own source, which reads as a plain code block.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.description: One of `lr` | `td`; declares the intended flow and mirrors to `data-direction` (dual-form contract, `data-` wins, mirror deferred past parse via afterParse). The fence's own `graph LR`/`graph TD` line remains the renderer's source of truth — authored source is never rewritten. Anything other than `lr`/`td` falls back to `lr` with an author-facing warning.

tags.name: npl-ref
tags.summary: Display-only rendering of an NPL ref block: post-hoc reflection over a finished turn (assessment, improvements, validation, eval, fine-tune).
tags.description: Display-only rendering of an NPL ref block: post-hoc reflection over a finished turn (assessment, improvements, validation, eval, fine-tune).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: one of `full`, `compact`, optional — `full` renders each section as a labelled block; `compact` renders one emoji line per section. Any other value resolves to `full`, and the resolved variant mirrors to `data-variant` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse, like sem-note, so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes). The variant is read at upgrade; it is display-only and not switched after wiring.

tags.name: npl-rubric
tags.summary: Display-only weighted scoring rubric: one table of criteria, each with a weight and a score, plus an overall figure that is stated or computed from the weighted average.
tags.description: Display-only weighted scoring rubric: one table of criteria, each with a weight and a score, plus an overall figure that is stated or computed from the weighted average. Source: NPL rubric blocks. The component renders the table and owns no state; a criterion whose weight or score is missing or non-numeric is marked, kept visible, and excluded from the average, and the overall figure is marked (stated) or (computed) (Lit `NplRubric`, `src/lit/npl/npl-rubric.ts`).

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: (empty). Rendered as the table caption and mirrored to `data-title` (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

attributes.name: npl-overall-score
attributes.description: (optional, one) — `value`: number — default: the element's trimmed text (`value` wins when both are present). States the overall score; when absent or non-numeric the component computes the weighted average — sum(weight · score) ÷ sum(weight) over the criteria with a numeric weight AND score (all-zero weights ⇒ no figure).

tags.name: npl-section
tags.summary: Generic typed section for NPL prompt-section blocks (`src/lit/npl/npl-section.ts`): display-only chrome over untouched authored content — a labelled header for known types, a warning box for unknown o
tags.description: Generic typed section for NPL prompt-section blocks (`src/lit/npl/npl-section.ts`): display-only chrome over untouched authored content — a labelled header for known types, a warning box for unknown ones. Light DOM per the namespace recipe; content stays searchable/copyable.

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: required. One of the known section types: `alg`, `alg-pseudo`, `diagram`, `example`, `format`, `logic`, `note`, `syntax`, `template`. A missing or unknown value is never fatal: the section renders with the `npl-section-warning` class, its content plain, plus one author-facing warning per offending value.

tags.name: npl-thought
tags.summary: Typed associative thought bubble (source: NPL thought blocks).
tags.description: Typed associative thought bubble (source: NPL thought blocks). A display-only container whose typed children are `npl-thought` elements that carry a `type` attribute, one per NPL thought-block type (`src/lit/npl/npl-thought.ts`).

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: optional; One of the eleven NPL thought-block types (case-insensitive): `observation`, `tangent`, `question`, `relation`, `concern`, `affirmation`, `reflection`, `opportunity`, `aversion`, `interest`, `eval`.

tags.name: npl-vos
tags.summary: Display-only bracket for an NPL vector-of-self block (`src/lit/npl/npl-vos.ts`): the psychodynamic state an NPL persona brackets each substantive response with — id, ego, mood, super-ego, optional col
tags.description: Display-only bracket for an NPL vector-of-self block (`src/lit/npl/npl-vos.ts`): the psychodynamic state an NPL persona brackets each substantive response with — id, ego, mood, super-ego, optional collective (source: NPL `vos` blocks, npl-full.md "Psychodynamic State"). One component renders one bracket; `phase` marks which half of the bracket it is. When vector-of-self is active it subsumes standalone `<npl-mood>` — do not author both.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.description: One of `entry`, `exit`; rendered as the bracket label and mirrored to data-phase (dual-form contract; the mirror is deferred past parse via afterParse so a sem-source snapshot never sees runtime writes).

tags.name: sem-audiences
tags.summary: Two halves, one contract: a declaration block (`sem-audiences`) names the profiles a document knows about, and an `audience` qualifier says who each element is for.
tags.description: Two halves, one contract: a declaration block (`sem-audiences`) names the profiles a document knows about, and an `audience` qualifier says who each element is for. The reader picks a profile; the script hides what is not for them. Nothing is ever removed from the document, and extraction never looks at the result.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: (required, document-unique): the profile token that `audience` specs and the hash parameter refer to. It is an ordinary element id, so it shares the document's id space.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): human label; the id renders when absent.

attributes.name: implies
attributes.description: (optional, comma list): profiles this one satisfies as well. `operator implies reader` means an operator sees reader content. Closure is transitive; a cycle is an authoring error, warned once and broken.

tags.name: sem-browser
tags.summary: A chrome-like window that renders a SemText document live.
tags.description: A chrome-like window that renders a SemText document live. The element exists because the landing "The Idea" section needs a BROWSER tab that names its document (an address bar), looks like a window (the shared window-chrome standard), and still renders the deck as real, hydratable DOM rather than an isolated frame. It is the window-frame sibling of `sem-shell` and `sem-code`; all three build their chrome from `src/shared/window-chrome.ts`.

attributes.name: src
attributes.description: (optional): VFS path or URL of the SemText document to render. With no `src`, the element's authored children are the viewport content.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): tab-label override. Priority: `label`, then the document's `<title>`, then the `src` basename, then `untitled`.

attributes.name: resolve
attributes.description: (property only, not an attribute): a host-injected `(path) => string | null | Promise<string | null>` consulted for scheme-less paths (`demo/deck.sem.html`, not `/…` or `https://…`) before any fetch. Returning a string adopts it; returning null errors without fetching.

tags.name: sem-chronology
tags.summary: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline.
tags.description: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline. Each `sem-event` is one dated assertion: *at `when` (until `until`), this happened*, optionally carrying a lifecycle `status`. DOM order is chronological order; the vocabulary does not sort. `view-as` selects the timeline rail or a plain list and never changes what an event means.

attributes.name: when
attributes.description: (recommended): the event's date or period start, as the author wants a machine to see it (ISO-8601 preferred, free text allowed).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: (optional): `done | current | todo | blocked` — same vocabulary as `sem-step`. Absent means unannotated, **not** `todo`: an event is a record of something that happened, not a task.

tags.name: sem-code
tags.summary: A source listing with provenance.
tags.description: A source listing with provenance. The element exists because plain `<pre><code>` cannot carry a filename, a language, or a set of emphasised lines that a machine can read back, and because copy / wrap are reading affordances that need JS. The listing itself is **verbatim**: whitespace inside `<code>` is content, never normalised.

attributes.name: lang
attributes.description: (optional): language token, rendered as a badge.

attributes.name: mark
attributes.description: (optional): emphasised lines, 1-based, comma list of numbers and `a-b` ranges (`2,4-5`). Out-of-range entries are ignored.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `copy`, `wrap`; Unknown flags are ignored.

tags.name: sem-data-join
tags.summary: A declaration, not a rendered dataset: it materializes one extra bucket — the **inner join** of two named buckets on a single named key column — that queries can address by `name`.
tags.description: A declaration, not a rendered dataset: it materializes one extra bucket — the **inner join** of two named buckets on a single named key column — that queries can address by `name`. Placed directly inside a `sem-data-visualizer`; zero-JS it is invisible (there is nothing to read). Outer joins, multiple keys and non-equality joins are out of scope.

attributes.name: data-name
attributes.description: (alias `name`): required — bucket key of the join result; colliding with a source name is an authoring error.

attributes.name: data-left
attributes.description: (alias `left`): required — the left-hand bucket to join, by `data-name` reference.

attributes.name: data-right
attributes.description: (alias `right`): required — the other bucket to join, by `data-name` reference.

attributes.name: data-on
attributes.description: (alias `on`): required — the named key column; must exist (case-insensitive) in both buckets.

tags.name: sem-data-query
tags.summary: The editable default query: a direct declaration whose text body is one query in the read-only SQL subset (`SELECT … FROM <bucket> [WHERE] [ORDER BY] [LIMIT]`).
tags.description: The editable default query: a direct declaration whose text body is one query in the read-only SQL subset (`SELECT … FROM <bucket> [WHERE] [ORDER BY] [LIMIT]`). Placed directly inside a `sem-data-visualizer`; no JOIN in the grammar (joins are declarative via `sem-data-join`), no aggregates, no write path. Zero-JS the query text shows as ordinary text (it *is* the document's record of the default query).

tags.name: sem-data-source
tags.summary: One named data bucket inside a `sem-data-visualizer`.
tags.description: One named data bucket inside a `sem-data-visualizer`. Its payload is either the element's inline text body or the resource named by `source` (an empty body plus `source` is the file/API form; a non-empty inline body together with `source` is an authoring error, rendered as a clear error, never silently resolved). Formats: inline Markdown table, CSV (RFC 4180), a YAML subset, JSON, a SQL result-shape declaration, or a file/API load; zero-JS the authored text reads as pre-wrapped text.

attributes.name: data-name
attributes.description: free text — human label rendered as the table `caption`, and the bucket key every query, join and cross-source view reference resolves (exact, then case-insensitive, then normalized: lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to `-`, edge `-` trimmed).

attributes.name: data-format
attributes.description: (optional): one of `table`, `csv`, `yaml`, `json`, `sql` — payload syntax of the body or of the fetched resource; Unknown format is a clear inline error, never a silent blank.

attributes.name: data-type
attributes.description: (optional): one of `rows`, `yaml-schema` — structure declaration; (absent ⇒ the tier infers). rows ⇒ simple row/column definition via the per-column declaration attribute; yaml-schema ⇒ the payload is an OpenAPI-style YAML document whose nested objects flatten to dotted column paths.

attributes.name: data-columns
attributes.description: (optional): string — with `data-type="rows"`, the per-column declaration, a comma list of `name[:type][?]` (`?` = nullable; types `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `date`, `null`). Declared types override inference per column; inference fills any column the declaration omits.

attributes.name: source
attributes.description: (optional): string — URL of a relative/same-origin file or an absolute `http(s)` file/API endpoint; inline payload and `source` are mutually exclusive. `file://` is refused when the document itself is `file://`.

attributes.name: data-views
attributes.description: (optional): named views as `name=colspec; name=colspec` — `colspec` is `*` or a comma list of column names, matched case-insensitively; malformed segments are skipped (a typo hides a view, it never breaks the document).

attributes.name: data-view
attributes.description: (optional): view name — the default view. Resolution: `data-view` name ⇒ first declared view ⇒ implicit `all=*`.

attributes.name: data-header
attributes.description: (optional): one of `true`, `false`; csv only: `false` ⇒ the first row is data and headers synthesize `col-<n>`.

attributes.name: data-path
attributes.description: (optional): string — `json`/API only: dot/bracket path into a nested response (`data.items`, `rows[2].entries`) that flattens to the row array.

attributes.name: data-cache
attributes.description: (optional): one of `no`; `no` ⇒ skip the in-memory fetch cache (one fetch per URL per page load by default).

tags.name: sem-data-visualizer
tags.summary: The container for data-visualizer state: it wraps one or more `sem-data-source` children (plus optional `sem-data-join` and `sem-data-query` declaration children).
tags.description: The container for data-visualizer state: it wraps one or more `sem-data-source` children (plus optional `sem-data-join` and `sem-data-query` declaration children). It mints no records of its own — it is the unit of tier scanning, of the modal viewer, and of shared view/query state. Zero-JS it shows its source children unenhanced (the authored text reads as pre-wrapped text).

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: optional — names the container for the modal deep link (`#dv=<visualizer-id>`). The copy-link chrome prefers the container's id; with none it falls back to the container's sole named source (`#bucket=<name>`), and a container with neither mints no copy-link button.

tags.name: sem-detail
tags.summary: Prose with occludable content.
tags.description: Prose with occludable content. Recall-oriented prose, distinct from `sem-reveal` (block disclosure) and `sem-views` (perspective switching): same prose, a different interaction model per view. Each `sem-detail` is one prose passage; a `<highlight>` child marks a recall target (`[[cloze]]` sugar maps to `<highlight>`) — `<em>` in plain view, occluded and revealed per item in the `quiz` view (self-check model). `view-as` is display-only sugar (`plain` default, `quiz`): the prose is identical under both.

tags.name: sem-details
tags.summary: Prose with occludable content.
tags.description: Prose with occludable content. Recall-oriented prose, distinct from `sem-reveal` (block disclosure) and `sem-views` (perspective switching): same prose, a different interaction model per view. Each `sem-detail` is one prose passage; a `<highlight>` child marks a recall target (`[[cloze]]` sugar maps to `<highlight>`) — `<em>` in plain view, occluded and revealed per item in the `quiz` view (self-check model). `view-as` is display-only sugar (`plain` default, `quiz`): the prose is identical under both.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `plain` (default) | `quiz`. Display-only sugar — the prose is identical; quiz view additionally occludes highlights.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: on the container; `kind`, `tags` global. Facts may also carry `<highlight>` prompts (schema sem-facts), but occlusion wiring for prose lives here.

tags.name: sem-enhanced-document
tags.summary: Required root wrapper; delimits extraction scope.
tags.description: Exactly one per document when the vocabulary is used. Plain HTML inside stays ordinary HTML; extraction scopes to the wrapper when present, otherwise to <body>.

tags.name: sem-event
tags.summary: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline.
tags.description: An ordered sequence of dated events — a timeline. Each `sem-event` is one dated assertion: *at `when` (until `until`), this happened*, optionally carrying a lifecycle `status`. DOM order is chronological order; the vocabulary does not sort. `view-as` selects the timeline rail or a plain list and never changes what an event means.

tags.name: sem-fact
tags.summary: A collection of fact/claim pairs.
tags.description: A collection of fact/claim pairs. Each `sem-fact` is an assertable statement/conclusion pair — the atomic citable unit (`id` is the citation token; `kind`, `tags` global). `view-as` is a **presentation parameterization, not a semantic change**: the fact *is* a fact under every view; the view selects the recall interaction (list = read, flashcards = self-test, quiz = scored recall).

tags.name: sem-facts
tags.summary: A collection of fact/claim pairs.
tags.description: A collection of fact/claim pairs. Each `sem-fact` is an assertable statement/conclusion pair — the atomic citable unit (`id` is the citation token; `kind`, `tags` global). `view-as` is a **presentation parameterization, not a semantic change**: the fact *is* a fact under every view; the view selects the recall interaction (list = read, flashcards = self-test, quiz = scored recall).

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `list` (default) | `flashcards` | `quiz`. Canonical attribute; display-only sugar — machines extract the same pairs regardless of view.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: on the container and on facts: required for citation (`#auth-facts/f-rotate`); `kind`, `tags` global.

tags.name: sem-md
tags.summary: A block whose content is authored as **Markdown** and rendered to HTML in the browser.
tags.description: A block whose content is authored as **Markdown** and rendered to HTML in the browser. The element exists for the one kind of content that is cheaper to write as Markdown than as HTML and that a machine wants back as Markdown: tables above all, then headings, lists, emphasis, links, code and quotes. It is not a second authoring format for the vocabulary — a `sem-fact` is still written as a `sem-fact` — and it never fetches, never evaluates and never injects markup: the renderer builds DOM nodes from the parsed text, so anything that looks like HTML inside the Markdown is rendered as the characters that were typed.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional): `rendered` (default) or `raw` — the initial mode. **Mutable presentation**: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone) and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): comma flags from `toggle`, `copy`; default both, also when the attribute is present but empty. Unknown flags are ignored.

tags.name: sem-note
tags.summary: A callout — prose set beside the main flow (`role="note"`, light DOM, content searchable).
tags.description: A callout — prose set beside the main flow (`role="note"`, light DOM, content searchable). The body is the element's content; `variant` (`info` default | `warning` | `tip` | `danger`) selects the accent and label, `collapsed` hides the body behind a ten-word teaser that expands on click, and `view-as="margin"` floats the note as a right-gutter aside on wide viewports (inline otherwise, and in print) — CSS-only. `view-as` is never extracted: a margin note and an inline note yield the same record.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — the body is hidden behind a ten-word teaser (`.sem-note-summary`) that expands on click.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: presentation only. On wide viewports the note floats right beside the prose that follows it (width `--sem-margin-width`, default 14rem), inside the container; a document whose column has a gutter pushes it out with `--sem-margin-offset`. On narrow viewports and in print it reads inline as an ordinary callout. CSS-only — no handler, no chrome, no record change.

tags.name: sem-option
tags.summary: Quiz answer candidate; correct marks the right one.
tags.description: Sugar: ✅ / ✗ prefixes mark correct / distractor options. Tier-1 demo element — the validator's schema does not know it yet.

tags.name: sem-procedure
tags.summary: An ordered, status-annotated procedure.
tags.description: An ordered, status-annotated procedure. Children: one `sem-step` per instruction, each carrying a `status` attribute. A step's `status` is its lifecycle annotation — `done` | `current` | `todo` default | `blocked`; DOM order is execution order — no step-number attribute, ordinals are positional and rendered with CSS counters. Status sugar (`✅/→/❌`) is display-only: `status` is canonical. Zero-JS element — pure CSS rendering. `kind` is a free token (`runbook`, `recipe`, `migration` …).

tags.name: sem-profile
tags.summary: Two halves, one contract: a declaration block (`sem-audiences`) names the profiles a document knows about, and an `audience` qualifier says who each element is for.
tags.description: Two halves, one contract: a declaration block (`sem-audiences`) names the profiles a document knows about, and an `audience` qualifier says who each element is for. The reader picks a profile; the script hides what is not for them. Nothing is ever removed from the document, and extraction never looks at the result.

tags.name: sem-progress
tags.summary: A completion meter — one scalar completion assertion.
tags.description: A completion meter — one scalar completion assertion. `value` is required, canonical unit 0..1: out-of-range values clamp for rendering while the raw attribute stays untouched; `label` is optional (default `progress`). The runtime builds a meter (track + fill + `label :: N%`); JS-off the value reads as text via CSS `attr()` — no fake bar. `status="done"` ⇔ value 1 by convention.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: required, canonical unit 0..1. Out-of-range values clamp for rendering; the raw attr stays untouched (machine readers see the author's value, the render shows the clamp).

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: optional completion state — pairs with value 1 and renders the full/accent state (same catalog as `sem-step`).

tags.name: sem-properties
tags.summary: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions.
tags.description: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions. Each `sem-property` is one pair — `key` is the term (required, free text), the property text is the value. Renders a `<dl>`-equivalent grid, zero-JS: the key column renders via CSS `attr(key)`, and each property authored as `role="definition"` + `aria-label` = the key lets AT announce the pair without JS. Compact `term :: value` sugar is display-only — `key` is canonical. Pure definition list, no copy/search chrome; `view-as="glossary"` turns the block into a glossary (term anchors get hover/focus preview popovers).

attributes.name: key
attributes.description: (on each `sem-property`): required, free text (the term). The property text is the value.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: (optional; R/W1): the block is a glossary. Each property should carry an `id`; prose elsewhere links a term with a plain anchor (`JWT`), optionally wrapping it in `` at its defining use.

tags.name: sem-property
tags.summary: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions.
tags.description: A definition/properties block: a closed set of key/value assertions. Each `sem-property` is one pair — `key` is the term (required, free text), the property text is the value. Renders a `<dl>`-equivalent grid, zero-JS: the key column renders via CSS `attr(key)`, and each property authored as `role="definition"` + `aria-label` = the key lets AT announce the pair without JS. Compact `term :: value` sugar is display-only — `key` is canonical. Pure definition list, no copy/search chrome; `view-as="glossary"` turns the block into a glossary (term anchors get hover/focus preview popovers).

tags.name: sem-question
tags.summary: Quiz block (Tier 1 demo element).
tags.description: Children: a prompt and sem-option candidates. Tier-1 demo element — no tier ships a handler yet, and the validator's schema does not know it yet.

tags.name: sem-reader
tags.summary: The reading chrome of a long document: an outline, a reading-progress bar, and the reader-side controls a printed page cannot offer — focus mode, type size and face, colour scheme, print, audience.
tags.description: The reading chrome of a long document: an outline, a reading-progress bar, and the reader-side controls a printed page cannot offer — focus mode, type size and face, colour scheme, print, audience. It is **chrome, not content**: it mints no record, its outline is derived from the document's headings, and a document without it loses nothing a machine could read. It exists as one element (rather than one per control) because every control shares a host, a persistence policy and an a11y contract, and because the planned `sem-themes` picker collapses into its `theme` control (R/W3 — not in this wave).

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: optional. Comma flags, in any order, one of `outline`, `progress`, `focus`, `type`, `color`, `print`, `audience` — unknown flags, including the theme flag reserved for R/W3, are ignored. Controls render in the **canonical order** above, not in attribute order.

attributes.name: outline-depth
attributes.description: optional. Deepest heading level in the generated outline, `2`–`6`; The outline always starts at `h2` — `h1` is the document title.

tags.name: sem-reference
tags.summary: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites.
tags.description: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites. Each `sem-reference` is one citable entry with an `id`; **inline citations are plain anchors** (`<a href="#r1">`) and mint nothing. The element exists because a reference needs fields a `<li>` cannot carry (`href`, `cite`) and because backlinks and hover previews are reading affordances that need JS.

tags.name: sem-references
tags.summary: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites.
tags.description: A numbered list of works or notes the prose cites. Each `sem-reference` is one citable entry with an `id`; **inline citations are plain anchors** (`<a href="#r1">`) and mint nothing. The element exists because a reference needs fields a `<li>` cannot carry (`href`, `cite`) and because backlinks and hover previews are reading affordances that need JS.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.description: `footnotes` | `bibliography` (free token; these two get distinct styling). Optional.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: (required; on each `sem-reference`): the citation target — the global `id`.

attributes.name: href
attributes.description: (optional; on each `sem-reference`): external location (`data-href` in the class form).

tags.name: sem-reveal
tags.summary: A Q→A disclosure, `<details>`-backed — the non-assertive counterpart to the `sem-fact` Q/A shape (a reveal is exposition, not an assertion).
tags.description: A Q→A disclosure, `<details>`-backed — the non-assertive counterpart to the `sem-fact` Q/A shape (a reveal is exposition, not an assertion). `summary` labels the closed state; when absent the leading body text (max 60 chars, cut at the last word boundary) derives it, by the one rule in `src/shared/summary.ts` that render and extraction share. `collapsed` starts hidden; without it the reveal starts open. The runtime's fallback handler — this element has no Lit component, like `sem-views` and `sem-progress` — wraps the element in native `<details>/<summary>`: click/keyboard toggling is the platform's; JS-off the content is fully visible (summary as a small-caps heading).

attributes.name: summary
attributes.description: optional label for the closed state. Default: the leading body text (max 60 chars, cut at the last word boundary, trailing punctuation dropped) acts as summary when absent.

attributes.name: collapsed
attributes.description: boolean attr — starts hidden (the `sem-note[collapsed]` convention carries over). Without it the reveal starts **open**.

tags.name: sem-source
tags.summary: A transparent wrapper around ordinary SemText content: the reader can flip between the section as rendered and its markup as parsed, before any enhancement.
tags.description: A transparent wrapper around ordinary SemText content: the reader can flip between the section as rendered and its markup as parsed, before any enhancement. It exists for documents that teach or demonstrate the vocabulary: the reader sees what a fact deck renders as, then sees exactly what was written to get it, without a second copy of the markup that could drift. It is a wrapper, not content: it mints no record, its children extract exactly as they would without it, and a document without it loses nothing a machine could read. The verbatim source is the one thing it adds, and that is a derived view of the children, never a second authoring.

attributes.name: view-as
attributes.description: `html` (default) | `source`. The initial mode. Mutable presentation: the toggle rewrites `data-view-as` at runtime (the authored bare attribute is left alone), and extraction ignores it (spec/extraction.md §5c).

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: (optional): a short caption rendered in the chrome.

tags.name: sem-step
tags.summary: An ordered, status-annotated procedure.
tags.description: An ordered, status-annotated procedure. Children: one `sem-step` per instruction, each carrying a `status` attribute. A step's `status` is its lifecycle annotation — `done` | `current` | `todo` default | `blocked`; DOM order is execution order — no step-number attribute, ordinals are positional and rendered with CSS counters. Status sugar (`✅/→/❌`) is display-only: `status` is canonical. Zero-JS element — pure CSS rendering. `kind` is a free token (`runbook`, `recipe`, `migration` …).

tags.name: sem-table
tags.summary: A data table a reader can sort and filter, whose **authored `<table>` is the contract**.
tags.description: A data table a reader can sort and filter, whose **authored `<table>` is the contract**. There is no JSON payload (PRD §5 planned one; it is dropped): the markup a person reads is the data a machine reads, which is the only way the extraction invariant can hold over a surface the reader reorders. The element exists because sort and filter are interactions, and because a machine reader needs the authored row order back after the DOM has been reordered — plain `<table kind="…">` covers a table nobody sorts.

attributes.name: data-value
attributes.description: (optional, on `<td>`): the sort key for that cell when the visible text is not the key (`15 min` vs `900`). Two numeric keys compare numerically; anything else compares as text, locale-aware.

attributes.name: controls
attributes.description: (optional): one of the comma flags `sort`, `filter`; Unknown flags are ignored.

attributes.name: sticky
attributes.description: (boolean, optional): the header row sticks to the top of the scroll container. Opting in also caps the element at `max-height: 24rem` so a long table scrolls inside itself — the stick needs an internal scroll container to engage, and without it a page-level table never gains one and the header would scroll away like any other row. CSS only — works with scripts off.

tags.name: sem-view
tags.summary: `sem-views` holds one subject under named perspectives: a tab bar of `sem-view` names shows one view at a time; with no script all views render stacked under their names.
tags.description: `sem-views` holds one subject under named perspectives: a tab bar of `sem-view` names shows one view at a time; with no script all views render stacked under their names. Switching is by click, arrow keys or hash, and never moves or rewrites the content itself. ❓ Q3 resolved for v1: **`sem-views`** (not `sem-perspectives`) — shorter, `name` reads naturally, tab-family semantics are the intent.

tags.name: sem-views
tags.summary: `sem-views` holds one subject under named perspectives: a tab bar of `sem-view` names shows one view at a time; with no script all views render stacked under their names.
tags.description: `sem-views` holds one subject under named perspectives: a tab bar of `sem-view` names shows one view at a time; with no script all views render stacked under their names. Switching is by click, arrow keys or hash, and never moves or rewrites the content itself. ❓ Q3 resolved for v1: **`sem-views`** (not `sem-perspectives`) — shorter, `name` reads naturally, tab-family semantics are the intent.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: required, unique within the container, human label.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: boolean marker on the initially-visible view; **if no view carries it, the first view is active**. The shown view is tracked at runtime in `data-active` (the component mirrors an authored `active` there, then moves it on every switch); the authored attribute is never rewritten.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: required **for enhancement, not only for deep links** — the handler selects `.sem-views[id]`, so a container without an id never upgrades and stays stacked (the JS-off form) even with script running. Also the deep-link head (`#deploy/argocd`); `kind`, `tags` global.

tags.name: statement
tags.summary: Fact part — the prompt side of a sem-fact.
tags.description: Bare semantic child of sem-fact; any inline content.
